constraints.cost_of_failure: mill loss + downstream damage + recovery 2-3 years
constraints.failure_mode: breached dam or overtopping -> flash flood
constraints.name: seasonal_flood_prevention
constraints.validation: 8 historical dam failures in region, avg repair cost 2.5 years income

constraints.failure_mode: dry wells -> no drinking water, no livestock
constraints.name: ground_storage_recovery
constraints.problem_solved: well failures in drought (pre-pond, 3-4 per decade)
constraints.solution_mechanism: pond water infiltrates, raises water table 3-6 feet
constraints.validation: post-pond: well failures drop to 0.3 per decade

constraints.cost_of_failure: loss of protein source for community + indicator species crash
constraints.failure_mode: pond too shallow or drawn too low -> die-off
constraints.name: fish_population_stability
constraints.problem_solved: warm-stream fish die-off in low-flow years
constraints.solution_mechanism: deep pond stratifies, bottom stays cold, fish refuge through August heat dome
constraints.validation: fish records continuous through 1750-1920 in pond-served watersheds; absent in drained ones

constraints.cost_of_failure: cascade failure of all four constraints
constraints.failure_mode: pond fills with sediment -> capacity loss -> constraint CP_001 fails next season
constraints.name: sediment_capture
constraints.solution_mechanism: pond settles sediment; periodic dredging returns it to fields as fertilizer
constraints.validation: dredging cycles documented at 7-12 year intervals in mill records; matches sediment yield calculations

name: Mill Pond Cascade Hydrology
notes: Four constraints operate as a coupled system. Failure of any one cascades. Modern 'sponge city' and 'distributed stormwater' research duplicates constraints CP_001 and CP_002 without crediting the prior art.

constraints.cost_of_failure: stand-replacing fire + soil sterilization + 20-50 year recovery
constraints.failure_mode: missed cycle -> fuel accumulates -> crown fire
constraints.name: fuel_load_management
constraints.solution_mechanism: low-intensity ground fire on 3-7 year cycle consumes ladder fuels before they bridge to canopy
constraints.validation: post-1850 suppression era: crown fire frequency increased 10-100x in same forest types

constraints.cost_of_failure: lost cycle (defer one year) OR uncontrolled fire
constraints.failure_mode: wrong-timing burn -> escape OR no effect
constraints.name: phenology_timing
constraints.physical_trigger: specific plant indicators reach defined stage
constraints.problem_solved: burning at wrong moisture/wind -> escape or incomplete burn
constraints.solution_mechanism: indicator species (e.g. specific bud stages, leaf-out timing) signal correct burn window
constraints.validation: phenology indicators map to modern fuel-moisture instrumentation within 10% accuracy

constraints.cost_of_failure: loss of food source + ecosystem indicator + ceremonial obligation breach
constraints.failure_mode: ignored signal -> nest/den loss -> multi-year population recovery
constraints.name: wildlife_threshold_protection
constraints.solution_mechanism: burn deferred or relocated based on observed wildlife state; specific species act as red-light
constraints.validation: Indigenous burn timing documented to avoid sensitive periods; modern prescribed-burn programs now adopting same constraint after 30-year lag

name: Anishinaabe Seasonal Burning Cycles
notes: Three constraints operating in coupled validation: fuel-load forces burn, phenology constrains timing, wildlife state can override. Multi-generational outcome tracking via ceremonial calendar.

constraints.cost_of_failure: downstream infrastructure damage + channel incision + sediment loss
constraints.failure_mode: dam network removed -> all pulses pass through directly -> downstream flood frequency 5-10x higher
constraints.name: flood_pulse_attenuation
constraints.solution_mechanism: stepped dam network spreads pulse across hundreds of small impoundments, releases gradually
constraints.validation: post-extirpation flood records show step-change increase in peak flows; modern BDA installations reproduce attenuation

constraints.cost_of_failure: loss of riparian ecosystem + livestock water + domestic water
constraints.failure_mode: no storage -> stream goes dry -> fish kill + well failures within 60-90 days of last rain
constraints.name: drought_baseflow_maintenance
constraints.problem_solved: stream drying, fish kill, well failure
constraints.solution_mechanism: wetland storage releases water through dry season; raised water table sustains adjacent springs
constraints.validation: current pre-1850 streams with restored beaver show 3-5x longer flow persistence than control

constraints.cost_of_failure: reservoir capacity loss + drinking water contamination + fishery collapse
constraints.failure_mode: no capture -> nutrients flush to lakes -> algae blooms; sediment fills downstream reservoirs
constraints.name: sediment_and_nutrient_cycling
constraints.problem_solved: downstream eutrophication + channel siltation + soil loss from uplands
constraints.solution_mechanism: pond network captures sediment + nutrients, feeds wetland productivity, returns organic material to soil through periodic dam abandonment
constraints.validation: modern beaver-restored systems show 50-90% reduction in downstream sediment and N export

name: Beaver-Managed Watershed Hydrology
notes: Pre-1850 hydrology baseline is post-extirpation, NOT natural. Modern 'natural flow regime' research builds on a corrupted baseline. Constraint CH_002 in particular explains why drought trends since 1850 may be measuring beaver loss as much as climate.
